findings.reason: a node that reads the raw pointer field computes `now - predecessor_start` (hours), reads the run as past the grace, and reproduces the very `halted` row §36 exists to remove; naming the resolver removes the ambiguity the plan's own §34 already warns about.
findings.text: the deliverable names the attempt's own start as "(`attempt_started_at`)", the raw field name, but inside the resume window that field on the pointer holds the *predecessor's* moment; the module it cites says so in the helper's own docstring — "Reading the pointer first therefore dates a just-resumed run from its predecessor, so the predecessor's quiet reads as the run's own and it is drawn stalled" (`reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:444-446`) — and the resolver that takes the later of the pointer's field and `attempt.json`'s is `_attempt_started_seconds`, which §34 (the rule §36 says it keeps) names explicitly

findings.reason: as written the first case may already read not-halted on the unfixed tree (the fix's positive case cannot fail), and the negative control ("with the previous attempt's stream deciding liveness again, the first case reads halted") has no named property to restore; the plan should state what makes the fixture's stream decide liveness — its last record, or the absence of an assistant record — since the plan itself defers "which branch produced `halted`" to the node.
findings.text: the fixture is specified only as a run "whose previous attempt delivered a complete manifest and whose stream has been quiet past the stall window", but stream *quiet* is capped at the current attempt's own clock by `_run_stream_quiet_seconds` (`min(quiet, launch)`, `reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:641-649`), so with an attempt started one second earlier the quiet reading is ~1 s regardless of the stream's age and the stated condition is inert; what actually decides the reading through `process_gone → _newest_stream_in_motion` is `_newest_stream_shows_work`, i.e. whether the predecessor's stream holds an assistant turn (`reckon/crew/recovery_wait.py:1168-1181`), and a delivered attempt's stream does
